local_candidates.title: GKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Security Analysis
local_candidates.description: All traditional encryption schemes share a fundamental operational vulnerability: encrypted data must be decrypted before it can be used. Fully homomorphic encryption eliminates this vulnerability by enabling computation directly on encrypted data, but existing FHE schemes impose substantial practical constraints that limit deployment. This paper presents a formal security analysis of the Gribov-Kahrobaei-Shpilrain (GKS) private-key FHE scheme. GKS requires no bootstrapping or de-linearization, produces bit-exact decryption, supports native encrypted search, and scales to unbounded depth.

local_candidates.title: Silent Blindness: Fault Vulnerability of Hardware Malware Detectors
local_candidates.description: Hardware malware detectors (HMDs) classify hardware performance-counter measurements to identify malicious execution. Faults in their decision logic or parameters can weaken detection and allow malware to be classified as benign. We investigate this vulnerability through structural fault injection across a design space comprising 18 classifiers, four counter budgets, and AdaBoost and Bagging ensembles. The simulation evaluates 453,174 decision stuck-at and selected parameter bit-flip events on a 7,400-instance. Primary comparisons use 128 completed configurations. These completed-subset results are distinguished from the simulation summaries covering 140 configurations with enumerable fault sites. Fault outcomes are classified by their security consequences, including evasion, false-alarm increases, and metric silence. A fault is critical when malware recall decreases by at least five percentage points. Tree-based models exhibit a lower mean critical-fault fraction than function-based models, 5.3% versus 14.3%; exhaustive-only analysis preserves this ordering. Moreover, 72.3% of evaluated tree faults are metric-silent, changing both recall and false-positive rate by less than 0.1 percentage points without necessarily preserving individual predictions. Among the 27 completed matched comparisons, Bagging reduces criticality in 26, whereas AdaBoost increases it in two. Finally, an exact minimax selection method identifies protection candidates under additive unit costs and ideal correction. For a representative J48 detector, protecting 16 of 115 structural units reduces predicted maximum recall loss from 60.1 to 3.3 percentage points. These results characterize structural-model sensitivity and potential protection benefits; faulted RTL correspondence and physical hardening overhead remain unvalidated.

local_candidates.title: SecDMP: Provably Secure Data Memory-Dependent Prefetching (Extended Version)
local_candidates.description: Data memory-dependent prefetchers (DMPs) are a microarchitectural optimization recently introduced in mainstream desktop and server CPUs. Although DMPs offer performance improvements, they have been shown to enable side-channel leakage of secrets, even from constant-time code that has been hardened against Spectre attacks. Unfortunately, existing defenses either incur significant performance overhead or, as we show, fail to prevent all DMP leakage. In this work, we address this gap by designing a defense that is both secure and efficient. First, we propose a classification of DMP leakage, categorize existing and novel attacks, and analyze which leakage classes are mitigated by existing defenses. We validate this analysis empirically by implementing the first open-source DMPs on a RISC-V processor, showing that the only existing defense that aims to preserve DMP performance fails to protect against entire leakage classes. Next, we propose SecDMP, a provably secure and efficient hardware-based defense. SecDMP requires secrets to be marked in memory and ensures that DMPs never encode these secrets in the microarchitecture---without compromising performance for public data. We formally prove that SecDMP introduces no leakage beyond a baseline semantics without DMPs. Notably, when combined with speculative-execution defenses, SecDMP restores complete microarchitectural security for constant-time code. Finally, our empirical evaluation shows that SecDMP prevents all DMP leakage while incurring minimal performance overhead and hardware cost.

local_candidates.title: Digital Data Protection Laws : A Review
local_candidates.description: Over the past couple of years, India has noted the significance of digital data and its protection. This article talks about the arising and present regime of India’s laws on digital data protection, specifically diving into the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. This act has tried to balance the scales between individual privacy rights and the economic growth that needs to be brought about by data-driven economic progress. A comparative study regarding data protection laws in the UK and US have been established, and this has been compared with DPDP 2023 in order to provide suggestions for improvements for the act. This paper examines various provisions, objects, and shortcomings of the DPDP Act, bringing into sharper focus areas of concern, notably government exemptions, data localization, and inadequacies in regard to a strong data protection authority. The article concludes with comparative analysis to shed light on strengthening the data protection regime in India and also makes some recommendations for future legislation in the light of emerging technologies like AI.

local_candidates.title: Developing a Dynamic Multi-factor Authentication System for Securing Smart Organizations
local_candidates.description: As smart organizations increasingly rely on technologies like AI, big data, and IoT, securing these systems is crucial. This research introduces a dynamic multi-factor authentication (MFA) system within the Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) framework, which enforces continuous verification. The system randomly selects biometric authentication factors, such as fingerprint, iris, and face recognition using a Markov chain model to ensure adaptability and reduce predictability in security measures. Using CASIA biometric datasets and AES-128 encryption, the system securely manages user data and authentication. Performance analysis shows that the dynamic selection process balances security and efficiency, making it suitable for smart organizations, particularly in e-government contexts. This MFA system strengthens cybersecurity by providing a flexible, real-time defense against evolving threats.

live_candidates.title: FPGA Implementation of the AES Algorithm with Lightweight LFSR-Based Approach and Optimized Key Expansion
live_candidates.description: Cryptography is essential for ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, and non-repudiation of information in the digital age. live_candidates.title: High-Performance and Area-Efficient VLSI Architecture for Secure Data Encryption Using AES Algorithm
live_candidates.description: In today’s rapidly evolving digital ecosystem, the protection of sensitive data has become a critical requirement for applications such as cloud computing, Internet of Things (IoT), embedded systems, and secure communication networks. The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is widely adopted due to its strong security and standardization; however, software-based AES implementations often suffer from high latency, limited throughput, and increased power consumption, making them unsuitable for real-time and resource-constrained environments. This work presents a high-performance and area-efficient VLSI architecture for AES-128 encryption, specifically optimized for FPGA-based platforms. The proposed design is implemented using Verilog HDL and realized on a Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA. A sequential, round-based architecture is employed to achieve an optimal balance between performance, area utilization, and power efficiency. To reduce hardware overhead, a memory-based S-Box implementation using Block RAM is adopted, significantly minimizing logic duplication and resource consumption. Core AES transformations—SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey, and Key Expansion—are modularly designed and controlled using a finite state machine (FSM). Functional correctness is validated using standard AES test vectors, while synthesis and timing analysis are carried out using Xilinx ISE and Cadence Genus. The results confirm that the proposed architecture is well-suited for real-time encryption in embedded and low-power systems. By offering a balance between performance and resource efficiency, the proposed AES architecture lays a strong foundation for future research and development in secure VLSI systems. Keywords: cryptography; VLSI; FPGA; AES; AES-128; Hardware Encryption; Verilog HDL Low Power; s-box optimization.

live_candidates.title: FSM-Based Area Efficient AES-128 Encryption Processor with Pipelined Round Architecture for FPGA Security Applications
live_candidates.description: The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is one of the most widely used symmetric key cryptographic algorithms for secure data communication in modern digital systems. With the rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT), embedded systems, and FPGA-based applications, there is an increasing demand for high-speed and area-efficient hardware encryption architectures. Traditional software-based encryption methods suffer from higher latency and lower performance, while fully pipelined hardware AES architectures consume significant hardware resources. This project presents the design and implementation of an FSM-Based Area-Efficient AES-128 Encryption Processor with a partially pipelined round architecture using Verilog HDL. The proposed design utilizes a finite state machine (FSM) to control the AES encryption process efficiently while reusing a single AES round block across multiple rounds to reduce hardware utilization. In addition, partial pipelining is introduced within the AES round operations to improve timing performance and throughput without significantly increasing the silicon area. The architecture consists of major AES transformation stages including SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey, and Key Expansion. A dedicated key expansion module dynamically generates all required round keys for AES-128 encryption. The entire design is verified using standard NIST AES test vectors, and the obtained ciphertext output matches the expected AES encryption results accurately. Simulation and waveform analysis are carried out using Icarus Verilog and GTKWave tools. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves a balanced trade-off between hardware area and encryption throughput, making it highly suitable for FPGA-based secure communication systems, embedded platforms, and resource-constrained IoT devices. The modular and scalable structure of the design also enables future enhancement toward AES-192, AES-256, and advanced low-power cryptographic architectures.

live_candidates.title: Hardware-Enhanced Protection for the Runtime Data Security in Embedded Systems
live_candidates.description: At present, the embedded systems are facing various kinds of attacks, especially for the data stored in the external memories. This paper presents a hardware-enhanced protection method to protect the data integrity and confidentiality at runtime, preventing the data from spoofing attack, splicing attack, replay attack, and some malicious analysis. For the integrity protection, the signature is calculated by the hardware implemented Lhash engine before the data sending off the chip, and the signature of the data block is recalculated and compared with the decrypted one at the load time. For the confidentiality protection, an AES encryption engine is used to generate the key stream, the plain data and the cipher data can translate through a simple XOR operation. The hardware cryptographic engines are optimized to work simultaneously with the memory access operation, which reduces the hardware overhead and the performance overhead. We implement the proposed architecture within OR1200 processor on Xilinx Virtex 5 FPGA platform. The experiment results show that the proposed hardware-enhanced protection method can preserve the integrity and confidentiality of the runtime data in the embedded systems with low power consumption and a marginal area footprint. The performance overhead is less than 2.27% according to the selected benchmarks.

live_candidates.title: Hardware-Based Protection for Data Security at Run-Time on Embedded Systems
live_candidates.description: The security of embedded systems has attracted much attention as they are being used in more and more fields. The rapid growth and pervasive use of embedded systems make it easier for a sophisticated attacker to gain physical access to launch physical attacks on insecure off-chip memory and bus. The proposed mechanism protects the confidentiality of data using advanced encryption standard (AES) stream encryption algorithm in parallel with the memory access process. This mechanism provides integrity protection for data by attaching integrity signatures generated using hash algorithm to data stored in external memory. The security architecture has been tested and validated on the system on a programmable chip (SoPC) with OR1200(processor based on OpenRISC1000 architecture) processor. live_candidates.title: SafeDB: Spark Acceleration on FPGA Clouds with Enclaved Data Processing and Bitstream Protection
live_candidates.description: This paper proposes SafeDB: Spark Acceleration on FPGA Clouds with Enclaved Data Processing and Bitstream Protection. SafeDB provides a comprehensive and systematic hardware-based security framework from the bitstream protection to data confidentiality, especially for the cloud environment. The AES key shared between FPGA and client for the bitstream encryption is generated in hard-wired logic using PKI and ECC. The data security is assured by the enclaved processing with encrypted data, meaning that the encrypted data is processed inside the FPGA fabric. Thus, no one in the system is able to look into clients' data because plaintext data are not exposed to memory and/or memory-mapped space. SafeDB is resistant not only to the side channel attack but to the attacks from malicious insiders. We have constructed an 8-node cluster prototype with Zynq UltraScale+ FPGAs to demonstrate the security, performance, and practicability.

live_candidates.title: Dynamic Scheduling of AES Cores for Aperiodic Tasks on Multi-tenant Cloud FPGAs
live_candidates.description: Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) have long been utilized in systems benefiting from hardware acceleration of processes unsuitable for execution on a traditional processor. Accordingly, as much of the world pivots from on-site datacenters and computing resources to hybrid or cloud based platforms, Multi-processing System-on-Chip (MPSoC) FPGAs are increasingly being employed in cloud computing systems to speed up many computation-intensive applications. In cloud computing, multi-tenant FPGAs are constantly space- and time-shared among multiple tenants dynamically by leveraging the partial reconfiguration property of FPGAs. With increasing security and privacy concerns introduced by these memory-based volatile devices, most countermeasures rely on encryption and decryption engines such as AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) cores for user data protection. However, their high-resource requirements and long latency limit the number of such engines that can be implemented in hardware. They often become a performance bottleneck during peak time. In this paper, we propose a scheduling algorithm for aperiodic tasks to dynamically share multiple AES cores and hence to improve their utilization and overall system performance. Extensive experimental measurements on an FPGA development board featuring a Xilinx Ultrascale+ FPGA demonstrate the efficacy of our mechanism.

live_candidates.title: DES encryption and decryption algorithm implementation based on FPGA
live_candidates.description: Nowadays there is a lot of importance given to data security on the internet. The DES is one of the most preferred block cipher encryption/decryption procedures used at present. This paper presents a high throughput reconfigurable hardware implementation of DES Encryption algorithm. This achieved by using a new proposed implementation of the DES algorithm using pipelined concept. The implementation of the proposed design is presented by using Spartan-3E (XC3S500E) family FPGAs and is one of the fastest hardware implementations with much greater security. At a clock frequency of 167.448MHz for encryption and 167.870MHz for decryption, it can encrypt or decrypt data blocks at a rate of 10688Mbps.
